analysis.title: Up and Adam
key_insights: The S&P 500 Technology sector fell 7.3% on Nov 5 to its lowest level since May 4 on concerns over data center regulation. Newly elected governors, rather than Congress, may have more direct control over data center approvals. Tech is 17% below its peak, in correction territory.

Raymond James says the risk of an eventual data center slowdown has increased, but underlying demand for AI solutions remains robust, and it expects the AI ecosystem to navigate the regulatory challenges.

The S&P 500 had its sharpest one-day drop since the April 2025 tariff turmoil, with all sectors lower. The index is 6% below its recent high. It historically averages 3.3 declines of more than 5% a year. In 2026 there have been two, none over 10%. Raymond James stays constructive on equities and views weakness as an opportunity for long-term investors, citing its positive earnings outlook.

The 10-year Treasury yield has fallen 53 bps from its 5.37% intraday peak a month ago, its highest level since 2002. Lower oil prices and concerns that a data center slowdown could weigh on growth are lifting bond demand.

Raymond James says Citi's Economic Surprise Index is near a three-year high and Treasury technicals show the fall in yields is stretched, so a near-term bounce would not be surprising. It expects the 10-year to drift to 4.50%-4.75% over the next 12 months.

Ahead of the BLS jobs report, job openings, ADP employment and ISM employment readings were generally upbeat despite sector-level weakness. Raymond James expects payrolls of +70k (September: 29k) with unemployment steady at 4.2%, and it continues to expect a Fed rate hike in December.

The 30-year mortgage rate has eased to 7.17% from a three-year high of 7.61% in early October, but is still about 120 bps above the start of 2026. New home sale prices fell 3.9% YoY as builders offered concessions. Raymond James says housing affordability challenges are not going away soon.
